Convert MusicXML to MIDI

What this does

MusicXML describes notation — notes, parts, articulations, layout. MIDI describes a performance — notes, velocity, tempo, channels. Converting one to the other gives you a file a DAW or sequencer can open and edit; notes, tempo and parts become a .mid file, while layout and lyrics do not carry over.

Open the converter with the format selected

How to convert

  1. Choose a .musicxml or .xml file.
  2. Set the output to MIDI (the default may not be MIDI, so select it manually).
  3. Convert, then Download.

What you get

Each part maps to a MIDI channel. Tempo changes written in the score are retained as tempo events. Lyrics, rehearsal marks, layout and other notation-only information are not carried over. Dynamics are approximated from score markings, not a real performance.

What MIDI cannot carry?

MIDI has no concept of a staccato dot, a slur or a page break. Only what a renderer can express as note timing or velocity survives the conversion, so articulations that do not affect timing are lost.

FAQ

Does the MIDI keep tempo changes?

Yes, tempo markings written in the score are exported as tempo events.

Why are some articulations missing?

MIDI has no concept of a staccato dot or a slur; only what the renderer can express as note timing or velocity survives.

Can I open the result in a DAW?

Yes — the file is a standard .mid and opens in Ableton, Logic, Reaper, MuseScore and most notation software.
